lecithin.compat-config.async-context-inh:
Let an async Bukkit task remember the execution context of the thread that created it, so a
legacy sync scheduler call made from inside that task can still be redispatched.
The owner is captured in CraftAsyncTask's constructor, which still runs on the thread that
asked, so it is a fact at that moment rather than something deduced later. Inheritance stops
after one hop and the thread's own context always wins when it has one.
Disabling this makes a legacy sync call from an async task fail closed again, exactly as on
stock Folia. Requires caller-context-dispatch.
lecithin.compat-config.async-event-prove:
Let an asynchronous Bukkit event that names exactly one online player stand as the execution
provenance for legacy sync scheduler calls made from inside its listeners; the task then goes
to that player's EntityScheduler, which is the documented API for scheduling one entity's work
from any thread. Paper dispatches AsyncPlayerChatEvent on a pooled thread that owns nothing, so
without this such a call has nowhere to go and takes the whole handler down with it.
Disabling this restores stock Folia rejection for those calls; no other dispatch path changes.
Requires caller-context-dispatch.
lecithin.compat-config.async-platform-ev:
The weaker half of async-event-provenance: an asynchronous event the platform itself defines
but which names no entity at all - the connection phase above all - is treated as server-scope,
and its legacy sync calls go to the global region. Kept separate so the strong claim (an event
that names one player belongs to that player) can stay on while this one is turned off.
The platform-package check is what stops this from becoming "any async caller gets the global
region": a plugin firing its own async event is still refused.
Disabling this makes those calls fail closed again. Requires async-event-provenance.
lecithin.compat-config.caller-context-di:
Run a sync Bukkit scheduler task that Folia rejects (scheduleSyncDelayedTask, runTask,
runTaskLater, callSyncMethod) on whatever the calling thread was already working on: a region
thread goes to that region's scheduler, the global region thread to the global scheduler, and
an entity-scoped context to that entity's scheduler. Nothing is inferred from the Runnable, and
a thread with no observable context is still rejected.
A task that reaches into state it does not own still fails loudly at that access; what changes
is only that a task which was never given a chance to run now runs.
Disabling this restores stock Folia rejection, which propagates out of the plugin's event
handler or onEnable and aborts everything after the call.
lecithin.compat-config.command-dispatch-:
Hand a console/RCON-sender Bukkit.dispatchCommand made from a region tick thread to the global
region, instead of refusing it where it was called. Folia already states that the global region
is where a console sender executes; this sends it exactly there. An Entity sender is untouched.
The parse stays on the calling thread, so Paper's only meaningful false (no such command) is
still returned synchronously; only the execution is deferred.
Not preserved: an exception thrown during execution no longer propagates out of the
dispatchCommand call - it surfaces on the global region on a later tick.
Disabling this makes such a dispatch throw out of the plugin's event handler again.
lecithin.compat-config.comment:
Compatibility with plugins and APIs written for a single main thread.
Every entry here is a separate switch over one specific gap between Paper and regionised
threading, and every one of them can be turned off individually to get stock Folia behaviour
back. None of them relaxes a thread-ownership or region check: work that genuinely touches
state it does not own still fails, loudly, at the access itself.
lecithin.compat-config.cross-region-bloc:
Answer a read-only block lookup from an already-loaded chunk when the calling tick thread does
not own that chunk's region, instead of refusing it. Every world builds its own regioniser, so
a thread ticking world A can never be the tick thread for a chunk in world B - a cross-world
read is not merely inconvenient but structurally impossible to satisfy otherwise.
Only resident chunks are served; nothing here can load, generate or tick a chunk, writes are
untouched, and threads that are not tick threads at all still fail so the async catcher keeps
working. The worst outcome is a block state one tick stale.
Disabling this restores the stock refusal.
lecithin.compat-config.diagnostics.comme:
Report Bukkit scheduler calls that Folia rejects as one attributable log record instead of a
message-less UnsupportedOperationException: plugin name and version, jar file and SHA-256, the
scheduler method actually called, delay/period, the sync/async flag, the plugin callsite and the
thread context - once per distinct callsite. Also covers the once-per-callsite notices for a
deferred teleport and a successful context redispatch.
Scheduling behaviour is unchanged either way; the call still throws.
Disabling this leaves the bare exception with no attribution.
lecithin.compat-config.economy-serializa:
Restore the per-account serialization Paper provided implicitly by having one main thread, for
plugin economy ledgers that keep a balance in a plain field and update it with a non-atomic
read-modify-write. On two region threads those updates interleave and one is silently lost -
with no exception and no ownership violation, because a money field is not world state.
It hooks two boundaries the server owns: Bukkit's ServicesManager (every Vault consumer resolves
the same provider object) and the legacy plugin command path. Different accounts still run fully
in parallel; no plugin bytecode is touched, and if the wrapping fails the original provider is
registered unchanged.
Disabling this leaves those ledgers racing.
lecithin.compat-config.paper-lib-environ:
Give an embedded PaperLib copy handlers that match this platform. PaperLib parses the server
version with a regex whose major-version group is a single digit, so on 26.2 the match fails,
the parsed version is 0, and it keeps its synchronous chunk and teleport fallbacks - the two
calls that cannot work across a region boundary. This is an upstream defect in PaperLib and it
misfires the same way on stock Paper 26.2.
Identification is structural (the class must be shaped like PaperLib), no bytecode is modified,
Bukkit.getVersion() is untouched, and PaperLib.isVersion(...) still returns its own honest answer.
Disabling this leaves every embedded copy with whatever handlers it selected for itself.
lecithin.compat-config.permission-lockin:
Take the class monitor in the two PaperPermissionManager methods Folia's synchronization sweep
missed: getDefaultPermissions(boolean), whose ImmutableSet.copyOf sizes an array and then fills
it - so a concurrent registration from another thread aborts the copy with
ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException - and removePermission(String). Two threads really do register
permissions during boot, and the server died there roughly one start in four.
Only a set copy runs under the monitor, so no lock-ordering edge is added.
Disabling this restores the unsynchronized bodies and the boot-time crash with them.
lecithin.compat-config.region-read-diagn:
Make an off-region block read fail attributably. Level#getBlockStateIfLoaded dereferences
getCurrentWorldData() with no null check, so a cross-region read ends in a
NullPointerException naming an unrelated field (captureTreeGeneration) rather than in the
thread-ownership message, which carries thread context, world and position.
The read already failed and still fails, at the same place, for the same reason; only the
exception's identity and diagnostics change.
Disabling this restores the misleading NullPointerException.
lecithin.compat-config.restore-async-sch:
Restore Bukkit's asynchronous scheduler. Folia replaces CraftScheduler.handle with an
unconditional throw, which also killed the async path - and that path never needed a main
thread, since Paper already runs those tasks on CraftAsyncScheduler's own pool. Sync tasks are
still rejected here; async tasks that illegally touch world state are still caught by the
thread-ownership checks.
Also restores the two guarantees the async path depends on: BukkitTask.cancel() no longer
throws after the cancel has taken effect, and disabling a plugin cancels its tasks again -
without that, a disabled plugin's async timers keep running its code until shutdown.
Disabling this makes every Bukkit scheduler call throw, async included.
lecithin.compat-config.riding-teleport.c:
Restore Paper's answer to teleporting an entity that is riding something else: dismount that
target, then move it, leaving the vehicle and any other passengers alone. Entity#teleportAsync
refuses outright when the target is a passenger and the Bukkit API always passes the passenger
flag, so every API teleport of a rider - boats, minecarts, horses, seats, mounts - returns false
and does nothing, and most callers discard the return value and cannot even notice.
A target whose teleport event is then cancelled is put back on its vehicle, like Paper.
Disabling this restores the platform's blanket refusal.
lecithin.compat-config.scoreboard-api.co:
Open the five Bukkit scoreboard methods Folia blocks with an unconditional throw, under region
rules rather than single-main-thread rules: plugin-created boards may be built and changed from
any tick thread (their broadcast path is thread-safe), the main scoreboard is persisted global
state so structural changes require the global tick thread, and assigning a board to a player
requires the thread that owns that player.
Neither check guesses an owner; both verify the current thread and fail loudly with attribution
when it is the wrong one.
Disabling this makes the five methods throw again.
lecithin.compat-config.server-current-ti:
Restore the MinecraftServer.currentTick field Folia commented out, advanced once per global
region tick - the successor of Paper's main-thread loop, and its single writer. Plugins that
read it reflectively from their NMS adapters (FastAsyncWorldEdit does) otherwise die on
NoSuchFieldError and take every one of their commands with them.
Disabling this removes the field's update; the field itself is only meaningful while this is on.
lecithin.compat-config.startup-context-d:
Treat the server bootstrap thread as global-region provenance for legacy sync scheduler calls,
so a plugin scheduling work from onEnable reaches the global region instead of being refused.
Region ticking has not started at that point, and the global region is where that work would run
once it does.
Disabling this makes such calls fail closed. Requires caller-context-dispatch.
lecithin.compat-config.startup-global-co:
Let the server bootstrap thread satisfy the global-region ownership check while the server is
still starting up. Region ticking only begins after initServer(), which is where world loading
and plugin onLoad/onEnable happen, so during startup the bootstrap thread is the sole owner of
global server state - exactly what Paper's main thread is at the same point. That thread is
itself a tick thread, so Bukkit.isPrimaryThread() already answers true on it and a plugin asking
the standard question was told yes and then rejected anyway.
Calls made after startup are rejected exactly as before.
Disabling this restores the stock rejection.
lecithin.compat-config.teleport-handover:
Let a teleport wait for the entity's previous teleport to finish handing it over to another
region, instead of being silently refused. A cross-region teleport does not move the entity, it
builds a copy and hands it to the destination region, which adds it to its lookup on a later
tick; in that window canTeleportAsync() refuses, so a plugin teleporting the same entity twice
in one tick gets true and then false and the second teleport never happens. Paper does both.
The teleport is scheduled on the entity's own EntityScheduler, which the platform transfers with
the entity; no owner is guessed and the calling thread does not wait.
Disabling this restores the plain refusal.
lecithin.compat-config.teleport-refusal-:
Print the four predicates behind a refused same-tick second teleport, plus removal reason,
callback class, ownership, both chunk states and the vehicle graph - and separately, the level
callback's NULL transitions. hasNullCallback() has no Bukkit API, so without this the reason for
the refusal cannot be read from outside.
Output only: it is called after the platform has already decided to refuse and returns void, so
it cannot influence the outcome. Prints on a refusal or a transition, never per tick.
Off by default; turning it on costs log volume only.
lecithin.compat-config.teleport-semantic:
Restore Entity#teleport(Location) and Player#teleport(Location) at the Bukkit API boundary.
Folia replaces both with an unconditional throw - not "throws when unsafe", but always, even
when the destination is a loaded chunk the calling thread already owns. The call is delegated to
the platform's own teleportAsync and its future is read without waiting: already completed means
Folia did the move inline and the real answer is returned, exactly as on Paper; not completed
means another region or world and the teleport was accepted but has not happened yet, which is
reported as true with a once-per-callsite notice.
No ownership check is bypassed and nothing is sent to the global scheduler.
Disabling this restores the unconditional throw from both classes.
lecithin.event-config.comment:
Bukkit events that Folia routes around and never fires.
These are notifications Paper plugins already listen for; restoring them changes which handlers
are called, not how the teleport itself is performed.
lecithin.event-config.passenger-teleport:
For a cross-world teleport, report each carried passenger's own offset position in its event
rather than the vehicle's, which is what Paper does there. Same-world teleports report the
vehicle's from/to on both platforms and are unaffected.
Disabling this gives every passenger the vehicle's position on cross-world teleports too - a
registered, harmless divergence from Paper.
Requires passenger-teleport-events.

Fire the teleport event for each passenger a teleported vehicle carries along. The platform
moves the whole tree but only the entity actually passed to teleportAsync gets an event, so a
player sitting in a boat, a minecart, a horse or a plugin seat crosses the world with no
teleport event at all - nothing that vetoes teleports is consulted and anything watching sees an
unexplained jump.
These events are notifications, not veto points: Paper ignores cancellation and setTo for a
carried passenger, and so does this, because honouring one passenger's veto could only produce a
half-moved tree.
Disabling this leaves the carried passengers silent again.
lecithin.event-config.teleport-events.co:
Fire PlayerTeleportEvent, EntityTeleportEvent and PlayerChangedWorldEvent, which Folia left as
a TODO when it routed every teleport through Entity#teleportAsync. Measured on the same script:
Paper fires PlayerTeleportEvent 3x and PlayerChangedWorldEvent 2x where this fork fired 0 and 0,
while the teleports themselves happened - so plugins that veto teleports or watch them are
simply never told.
The event is fired after the platform's own validity checks and before anything is mutated, on
the thread that owns the entity, so a cancel is a plain refusal with no lock to unwind, and
setTo is honoured including to another world. Teleports whose cause is UNKNOWN - the platform's
own internal repositioning, which has no Paper counterpart - are skipped.
Disabling this stops all three events again.
lecithin.waypoint.remake_connections.com:
Implement the waypoint manager's remakeConnections instead of throwing. It is not unused:
ServerScoreboard.updatePlayerWaypoint/updateTeamWaypoints call it on every team-membership or
team-colour change of an online player, because locator bar waypoints are team-coloured - so the
vanilla /team command and any plugin team change killed the caller. It mirrors vanilla's
ServerWaypointManager and recreates the connection for every tracking player; createConnection
already hops to the player's owning region.
Disabling this restores the throw, and with it the /team crash.
